articles.title: 魅族 22 手机限量补货开售：至高 3 期免息，16GB+512GB 国补价 3499 元起
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，魅族科技官方今日宣布，京东自营旗舰店，魅族 22 限量补货开售，至高享 3 期免息，叠加国补至高立减 500 元。京东魅族（meizu）22 16GB+512GB3999 元直达链接京东商品页显示，魅族 22 目前仅 16GB+512GB 有货，国补价 3499 元起（归航版 3999 元）。据IT之家此前报道，魅族 22 手机于今年 9 月 15 日发布，该机搭载第四代骁龙 8s 处理器、配备 1.5K 高刷无界屏（0.8mm 四等边“独白”面板）、采用 5000 万像素广角 + 5000 万像素 3 倍潜望长焦 + 5000 万像素超广角 + 5000 万像素前置镜头组合，定价 2999 元起。今年 2 月 27 日，魅族科技发布战略转型公告，宣布将暂停国内手机新产品自研硬件项目。前星纪魅族集团中国区 CMO 万志强 3 月 1 日在魅族京东自营店进行直播，期间透露了部分有关魅族未来的规划：魅族 22、魅族 Note 16 系列、魅族 Lucky 08 仍在正常售卖，后续也不会涨价；魅族 23 已完成开发，但是不会面向市场发售；魅族 22 的 1TB 版本官方渠道已售罄，魅族 22  归航版也所剩不多；后续 Flyme 系统不会再推出大版本更新，但会持续提供基本维护。▲ IT之家图赏：魅族 22京东魅族（meizu）22 16GB+512GB3999 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 科大讯飞 2026 年三季度归母净利润 2.26 亿元，同比增长 31.05%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，科大讯飞今日发布 2026 年三季度（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）报告：营业总收入：65.65 亿元，同比增长 7.99%归母净利润：2.26 亿元，同比增长 31.05%扣非净利润：-1.26 亿元，同比下降 580.7%加权平均净资产收益率：1.07%基本每股收益：0.0956 元，同比增长 28.32%稀释每股收益：0.0956 元，同比增长 28.32% AI 解读本次财报业绩符合市场预期，核心指标实现增长。公司主营业务说明科大讯飞聚焦智能语音、自然语言理解、多模态、通用人工智能等 AI 核心技术研究，推动人工智能产品研发和行业应用落地，在认知智能、语音及语言处理领域具备领先优势，主打讯飞星火大模型，已实现全栈国产化技术布局，在行业大模型领域具备较强竞争力。财报核心亮点第三季度实现营业收入 65.65 亿元，同比增长 7.99%，业务结构持续优化，虽然 G 端业务收入同比下降 2.39%，但智慧教育、智慧医疗业务均实现 20% 以上的良性增长，运营型业务取得显著进展。第三季度归属于上市公司股东的净利润达到 2.26 亿元，同比增长 31.05%，扣非归母净亏损为 1.26 亿元，同比下降 580.7%，主要系公司坚持自主可控技术路线，持续保持高强度研发投入。第三季度研发投入金额超 17 亿元，较去年同期增长近 4 亿元，占营业收入比重逾 25%，研发投入力度持续加大。年初至第三季度末，累计实现营业收入 181.87 亿元，同比增长 7.05%；累计实现归母净利润 2188.72 万元，同比增长 132.83%，累计经营活动现金流实现转正，达到 2.64 亿元，同比增长 115.28%。未来展望公司将于 10 月 22 日发布全新的“云 + 端”讯飞星火大模型，基于全国产算力底座全新升级端云一体化解决方案，并全新升级多模人机交互技术，以“Token+Agent”推动从能力开放到价值共创的星火生态升级。公司将继续坚守核心技术自主可控，加强大模型底座研发及软硬件一体化业务布局拓展，战略投入有所增长，契合公司长期战略发展规划。相关阅读： 《科大讯飞 2026 年上半年归母亏损 2.04 亿元，同比收窄 14.68%》《科大讯飞 2026 年半年度归母亏损 1.8 亿元～2.28 亿元，同比预增 5%~25%》《科大讯飞 2026 年一季度亏损 1.70 亿元，同比增长 12.17%》风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.title: 三星推出 Galaxy F70 5G 手机：Exynos 1330 处理器，6.7 英寸 90Hz AMOLED 屏幕
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，三星现已在印度市场推出 Galaxy F70 5G 手机。新品采用 Exynos 1330 处理器和 5000 万像素摄像头，起售价为 19,999 卢比（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,408 元人民币）。据介绍，这款手机的尺寸为 164.4*77.9*7.5 mm，重量 192g。正面配备一块 6.7 英寸 Super AMOLED 屏幕，分辨率为 2340*1080，支持 90Hz 高刷。官方宣称该机具备 IP54 级防尘防水能力，采用康宁大猩猩玻璃 Victus。同时，这款手机搭载三星自研 Exynos 1330 八核心处理器，提供 4GB/6GB 内存和 128GB 存储空间。该机内置 5000mAh 电池，支持 25W 有线充电。后置主摄为 5000 万像素，支持光学防抖，除此之外还带有 500 万像素超广角镜头，和 200 万像素微距镜头。此外，这款手机出厂运行基于 Android 15 的 One UI 7 系统，官方承诺提供四年 Android 大版本更新和五年安全补丁。

articles.title: 两部门对盾构机等物项实施出口管制，商务部回应称依法依规、符合国际通行做法
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，商务部、海关总署今日联合发布公告，对盾构机等物项实施出口管制、优化调整挖泥船相关物项出口管制措施。据央视新闻报道，商务部新闻发言人回应称：根据《中华人民共和国出口管制法》等有关法律法规，10 月 19 日，商务部会同相关部门发布关于对盾构机等物项实施出口管制、优化调整挖泥船相关物项出口管制措施的公告，并于 11 月 18 日起正式实施。此前，我们已经向与中方建立了出口管制对话机制的有关国家和地区作了通报。此次措施相关物项具有明显的军民两用属性，中国依法依规实施出口管制措施，符合国际通行做法，更好地维护了国家安全和利益，更好地履行了防扩散等国际义务。中国作为负责任大国，列管或优化调整相关管制措施，体现了坚定维护世界和平与地区稳定的一贯立场。中国政府愿与各国一道维护全球产供链稳定畅通，中方将依法依规对相关出口许可申请进行审查，对符合规定的申请，中方将予以批准。同时，中方愿通过双边出口管制对话交流机制，与相关方就出口管制政策和实践开展沟通对话，共同积极促进、便利合规贸易。IT之家从公告获悉，根据《中华人民共和国出口管制法》《中华人民共和国对外贸易法》《中华人民共和国海关法》《中华人民共和国两用物项出口管制条例》有关规定，为维护国家安全和利益，经国务院批准，决定对下列物项实施出口管制：一、掘进机相关物项（一）2B906．全断面隧道掘进机。a．土压平衡盾构机、泥水平衡盾构机及其他类型盾构机（参考海关商品编号：8430313010）；b．敞开式、单护盾、双护盾岩石隧道掘进机及其他类型岩石隧道掘进机（参考海关商品编号：8430313010）。（二）2A906．专门设计用于 2B906 项所管制物项的零部件：a．刀具刀盘（参考海关商品编号：8431499910）；b．螺旋输送机（参考海关商品编号：8428310010）；c．管片拼装机（参考海关商品编号：8479899959）；d．主驱动系统及其他关键单元（参考海关商品编号：8431499910）。（三）2E906．专门设计用于 2A906 或 2B906 项所管制物项的再制造技术。二、步履式挖掘机相关物项（一）2B904．具有以下任一特性的步履式挖掘机（参考海关商品编号：8429521920）：a．跨越垂直障碍高度超过 1.2 m；b．涉水深度超过 1.5 m；c．跨越壕沟宽度超过 3 m；d．步行爬坡度超过 40°。技术说明：步履式挖掘机是指利用工作装置、支腿或车轮的复合动作，实现自行走，从而在全通用地形开展多功能挖掘的机械设备。（二）2E904．专门设计用于 2B904 项所管制物项的液压系统电液比例控制技术。三、高原型湿喷机相关物项（一）2B903．用于海拔 3000 m 以上地区，具有以下所有特性的高原型湿喷机（参考海关商品编号：8479109010）：a．发动机最大功率超过 75 articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，韩媒 MTN 当地时间 16 日报道称，三星电子计划 2027 年全面进军硅光子学 (SiPh) 领域，首先利用 12 英寸技术为客户代工光子集成电路 (PIC)，后续则将扩展到 PIC-EIC 整合、光封装领域。台积电目前在硅光子学晶圆代工领域处于优势位置，已获得了一系列的开发成果。三星电子内部人士认为，企业与台积电在硅光子学方面的差距在于市场份额而不是技术本身。三星电子将以其从存储到逻辑到封装的全栈解决方案与台积电竞争。三星电子也在考虑对硅光子学相关公司进行合并和收购，以推进自身技术发展。

articles.title: 光荣特库摩将 2026 上半财年归母净利润预测上调一倍至 180 亿日元，同比预增 33.68%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，光荣特库摩今日发布 2026 财年半年报（2026 年 4 月 1 日～2026 年 9 月 30 日）业绩预告报告：营业总收入：370 亿日元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 15.68 亿元人民币），同比预增 18.33%归母净利润：180 亿日元（现汇率约合 7.63 亿元人民币），同比预增 33.68%基本每股收益：53.87 日元（现汇率约合 2.3 元人民币），同比预增 26.43% AI 解读本次业绩预告修正后核心指标均超出市场此前预期，盈利能力大幅上调。公司主营业务说明光荣特库摩是日本知名游戏开发与发行商，主营业务涵盖家用主机游戏、移动端游戏开发发行，IP 授权运营，旗下拥有《三国志》《仁王》《真三国无双》等知名 IP。本次财报业绩亮点修正后预计营业收入为 370 亿日元（现汇率约合 15.68 亿元人民币），较前回发表预测增加 30 亿日元（现汇率约合 1.27 亿元人民币），同比增长 8.8% ；修正后预计归属于母公司股东的中期净利润为 180 亿日元（现汇率约合 7.63 亿元人民币），较前回发表预测增加 90 亿日元（现汇率约合 3.81 亿元人民币），同比增长 100% ；修正后营业利润预计为 115 亿日元（现汇率约合 4.87 亿元人民币），经常利益预计为 250 亿日元（现汇率约合 10.59 亿元人民币），均较此前预测大幅上调。业绩上调原因本次业绩上调主要得益于前一年度发售的大型 Titles 和卡牌类游戏销售表现强劲，带动营收和营业利润增长；同时金融市场运用带来营业外收入超预期，推动经常利益和净利润进一步向上修正。未来展望截至目前，公司对全年连通业绩预告暂未做调整，后续将持续关注商业环境和金融市场动向，适时检讨更新业绩预测。风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.title: 划清界限：美国银行、摩根大通银行、嘉信理财等金融平台屏蔽 Muse 等智能体
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，一批用上 Meta Muse 等智能体的美国用户发现，自主式 AI 近期遭到多个金融平台封禁。嘉信理财（IT之家注：Charles Schwab）CEO 里克 · 沃斯特上周接受彭博采访时表示，他们每周都会拦截多种 AI 智能体，并定期收到相关报告。不过嘉信理财并未完全屏蔽外部 AI 智能体。外部模型可通过专用的 MCP 服务器查询账户余额和研究资料，不可执行资金转移等操作。这名 CEO 表示，封禁外部智能体的原因在于责任归属不明确，银行和客户都无法控制这些第三方智能体。一旦出现问题，究竟谁承担责任没有明确答案。摩根大通银行 CEO 杰米 · 戴蒙也在财报电话会议中谈到，他们不允许任何第三方智能体随意访问其系统。随后摩根大通发言人补充称，任何试图使用银行登录凭据登录的智能体都会遭到拒绝。美国银行也采取了类似的政策，禁止智能体进行转移资金等操作。除此之外，越来越多公司试图与智能体划清界限。达美航空已不再允许用户使用智能体预订航班，Yelp 只向付费的智能体服务提供商开放访问权限。早在今年 9 月，亚马逊就指责 Muse 违反了网站规则。根据用户反馈，xAI 的 Grok 和 OpenAI 新推出的常驻智能体 Dots 也无法在亚马逊上正常运行。

articles.title: 小米智能开关 2 Pro 开启众筹：AG 玻璃面板、多种控制方式，114 元起
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，小米智能开关 2 Pro 现已在有品开启众筹（点此访问），众筹价 114 元起，IT之家整理价格信息如下：单键：114 元双键：133 元三键：152 元系列产品定位仍是“把传统灯具接入智能家居”的入门级改造件：采用标准 86 底盒，可原位替换传统开关；官方重点放在单零火兼容、Mesh 2.0 组网、按键可转无线开关，以及对传统灯 / 智能灯的同时适配上。外观方面，这一代智能开关继续走“薄面板”路线。商品页称面板厚度控制在 3.5mm，并加入高强度钢片支架，强调安装后更贴合墙面、降低变形概率。表面为 AG 玻璃，叠加 AF 涂层，主打抗油污、耐指纹、防刮花，提供双色可选。按键部分改用微动开关，官方描述为按压清脆、回弹利落。安装兼容性方面，其支持“单零火兼容设计”，可根据家中线路条件自动呈现单零火不同操控界面，面向没有预留零线的老房改造场景，官方称无需改线、无需额外改造费用。同时，双键、三键版本可在米家 App 中为每个按键自由分配对应灯具，降低接错线后反复拆装调试的成本。连接与控制方面，小米智能开关 2 Pro 采用小米 Mesh 2.0 模组，官方宣称响应速度提升 50%、组网时间降低 50%，并支持远程自动 OTA。控制方式覆盖实体按键、米家 App 远程操作、小爱同学语音控制，同时标注支持小米澎湃智联与“已接入米家”。这部分功能依赖蓝牙 Mesh 网关，页面小字也提醒接入米家需搭配具备蓝牙 Mesh 网关能力的设备。场景化能力方面，官方给出的链路包括：开门自动亮灯，需要智能门锁、蓝牙 Mesh 网关、窗帘等配合；离家时一键关灯、开窗帘并联动扫地机器人。更实用的一项是“按键可转无线开关”—— 在无线模式下，按键不只控制灯，也能联动扫拖机器人、空气净化器等设备。安全与耐用参数方面，新品支持 10A 最大电流负载、2200W 负载能力，提供过温 / 过载保护；寿命宣传为“双百万”设计，对应 100 万次级别按压 / 通断指标。细节功能上，产品采用鞍型接线端子，强调齿型压线结构可兼顾单股与多股电线，降低安装伤线概率；同时支持用电量统计，可按日 / 周 / 月 / 年查看，适合对回路能耗敏感的用户。IT之家附产品参数：

articles.title: 微信鸿蒙版 App“两年狂奔”：交付 41 个大版本、344 个小版本，追上 iOS 端 15 年迭代进程
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，微信官方公众号“微信派”今日发文，回顾了鸿蒙版 App 的“两年狂奔”。据介绍，鸿蒙版以两年内交付了 41 个大版本、344 个小版本，平均每两天提审一个版本的速度追了上来。2024 年至今，微信从 0 把鸿蒙版更新到了 8.0 系列版本。但同样从 1.0 到 8.0，微信 iOS 版用了 15 年。▲ 源自微信官网版本更新数据微信官方称，鸿蒙的一切都是新的。面对全新的架构，全新的开发语言...... 过往十余年沉淀的经历在这里基本用不上。这也是为什么在 2024 年 3 月内部立项起初，微信就决定“放弃历史包袱，彻底重构”。即便是再老练的微信程序员，想要“再造微信”，也得深夜匿名在网站发帖求助。关于“为什么有些功能微信鸿蒙版上还没有？”这一问题，IT之家从微信官方了解到，鸿蒙版 App 用的方式是「先上尝鲜版，再公测，再正式上架」。面临一个全新的操作系统，它功能更新的过程，跟用户的预期之间会有一些差距。大家在IT之家微信号回复“微信”两字，即可获取当前最新官方内部版微信下载。

articles.title: 东风猛士 X700 车型 10 月 25 日上市：华为乾崑智驾 + 鸿蒙座舱，预售 24.98 万元起
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，据易车今日报道，猛士 X700 将于 10 月 25 日正式上市。新车共推出 3 款车型，预售价 24.98 万元起，搭载华为乾崑智驾 ADS 5 及鸿蒙座舱 HarmonySpace 6，是猛士品牌 X 系列的首款产品。据IT之家此前报道，猛士 X700 方盒子车型于 9 月 28 日开启预售，这是猛士品牌 X 系列的首款产品，搭载华为乾崑全栈智能，预售价 24.98 万元起：285KM 四驱 Max：预售价 24.98 万元285KM 四驱 Max+：预售价 26.98 万元360KM 四驱 Ultra：预售价 28.98 万元猛士 X700 长宽高为 5035×1999×1910mm，轴距 2920mm，定位中大型 SUV。新车提供 265/65R18 与 255/60R20 两种规格轮毂可选。猛士 X700 车顶配备 896 线激光雷达，延续猛士与华为乾崑全栈深度合作，支持高速 NOA、城市 NOA、记忆泊车等功能，还带来 AEB 3.0、车位到车位 3.0 等。动力方面，猛士 X700 提供增程版和插混版两种选择，均搭载 1497ml 发动机，增程版功率 95kW，最大净功率 90kW；插混版功率 113kW，最大净功率 110kW。该车采用 800V 平台架构，配备 68.1kWh 宁德时代越野专用电池，CLTC 纯电续航 360km；零百加速 4.93 秒，综合功率可达 518kW。

articles.title: SE 警告网游《最终幻想 14》日服出现大量账号异常登录情况，用户应密切关注密码安全
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，Square Enix 今天发布公告，称旗下在线 MMORPG《最终幻想 14》（Final Fantasy XIV）日服出现大量异常登录行为，提醒玩家检查账号安全，避免使用固定或容易被猜测的邮箱与密码组合。官方指出，这类异常登录行为可能与近期“日本企业遭黑客入侵潮”有关，2026 年 10 月以来，日本至少有 20 家大型企业、平台及公共系统遭到黑客非法访问，涉及汉堡王、烧肉王、订票平台 Skyticket、租车平台 Times Car 等。Square Enix 表示，对于疑似遭到未经授权访问的账号，官方将采取限制登录等措施，并通过电子邮件通知相关玩家。如果账号受到限制，玩家需要按照官方邮件中的说明完成验证并重置密码，才能解除限制。官方还提醒玩家，尽量避免在不同网站和服务中重复使用相同密码，并及时修改容易被猜测的密码。如果异常登录情况进一步扩大，Square Enix 不排除要求所有账号统一重置密码。

articles.title: Amkor 拟未来 5 年斥资 3 万亿韩元提升韩国光州先进封装产能
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，头部 OSAT 企业 Amkor（安靠）当地时间今日在其韩国光州工厂举行扩建项目奠基仪式。该项目将服务于 AI / HPC 芯片的先进封装需求。IT之家了解到，该项目投资规模达到 3 万亿韩元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 149.79 亿元人民币），将创造 3,000 个就业岗位，预计 2027H2 建成首批 2 座厂房、2028H1 建成另 2 座，此后开始批量生产。Amkor 总部当前位于美国，但其最早可追溯到一家韩国企业，韩国也是其全球产能布局的重要一环。Amkor 去年底在韩国仁川开始建设一家先进测试工厂。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，Counterpoint Research 最新数据显示，2026 年第三季度中国智能手机出货量同比下降 10%，创下 2012 年以来同期最低水平。而这背后主要是内存维持价格上涨、供应紧缩态势的影响。▲ 图源：Counterpoint从市占来看，华为与苹果合计占据 40.8% 出货量，较去年同期大幅提升。这显示出在内存成本上涨周期中，强大的高端市场布局能够带来明显的份额优势。随着旗舰智能手机移动平台的发布，2026 年 9 月迎来一波 Android 新机浪潮。几大制造商今年在“入门旗舰”档采取了不同的产品策略：小米 18 标准版延期发布、OPPO 推出 Find X10 E、荣耀则带来 Magic9 超能版。这些决策背后是制造商对价格和销量平衡的审慎考虑。当前成本通胀程度已经表明，越来越多的厂商无法完全消化更高的元件成本。涨价范围扩大后，消费者开始选择推迟换机、等待大促活动再购买，或者转向翻新市场选购更实惠的产品，这些行为会进一步削弱智能手机需求，给 2026Q4 的销售带来额外压力。参考China Smartphone Shipments Hit 14-Year Low in Q3; Huawei and Apple Buck the Downtrend

articles.content:

How do you feel about it? And did you find a solution to stay motivated to learn and get better at using AI?

articles.title: Git 被换掉，LLM 被替代：AI 编码开始反噬传统工具链？
articles.content: Anthropic 代码量暴涨，GitHub 密钥扫描又慢又贵，两家被迫改造系统。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       Git 已经支撑软件开发二十多年，Anthropic 却决定把它换掉。为了让 Claude 持续生成的代码顺利进入开发流程，7 名工程师花了 5 个月，开发出版本控制系统 Scion，并将核心代码仓库迁移过去。今年 5 月，Anthropic 每天平均合并约 2500 项代码变更，到 9 月已超过 3 万项，仅 CI 系统每天就要执行约 2500 万次代码检出。写代码的速度上来了，准备仓库、同步对象和查询历史却越来越费机器。几乎同一时期，GitHub 用微调后的 ModernBERT 替换密钥扫描中的通用 LLM 判断。哥伦比亚大学与 Google DeepMind 等机构则通过 BTTF，把芯片仿真波形转换成 SQLite，让 Agent 使用 SQL 排查异常。Scion 默认在线，BTTF 将波形变成查询接口，GitHub 把高频判断交给分类器。围绕人类开发节奏设计的系统，开始承受 Agent 带来的另一种负载。01Git 的离线能力，为什么成了负担Git 的分布式设计让工程师克隆仓库后，即使断网也能提交、合并、查看历史。但 Anthropic 大量读取代码的任务是始终联网的 CI 作业和 Agent 沙箱，运行几分钟便销毁，可能只需要几个文件、一份 diff，或确认两个提交的祖先关系。为了这些操作准备本地仓库，重复成本越来越高。Anthropic 主分支历史接近 100 GB，压缩工作副本超过 25 GB。若每天 2500 万次检出分别获取完整副本，理论流量会超过 600 PB。公司虽用浅克隆、稀疏检出、快照和数百台 Git 镜像，但镜像仍要同步、快照会过期，历史查询还需补齐对象。仓库越活跃，维护成本越高。Scion 将客户端缩成轻量入口。提交创建、合并、变基与历史查询放到中心服务，本地仅监测文件变化、维护少量缓存，需要工作目录时按需展开。CI 若只想计算 diff，可以直接调用 API，无须完整检出。这牺牲了离线自治，却减少重复初始化。提交格式也变了。Git commit 指向描述仓库状态的目录树，Scion 的 changeset 则以预写日志条目记录相对首个父提交修改过的文件，通过内容寻址指针引用数据。创建 changeset 无须生成 Git packfile，也不用立即移动共享分支，只有 main 等引用更新时，系统才对 Spanner 中的单行记录执行 compare-and-swap。Agent 可以并发生成变更，竞争集中到分支引用移动时。但历史查询仍有难题：增量记录无法直接回答某行是谁改的、文件经历过什么。Scion 为 blame、路径历史与提交图跳表维护 derived data，按父提交关系预计算，或等查询发生后再生成。写入与历史分析可以独立扩展。雷峰网检出时，scn 客户端从目标目录树开始，只请求缺失的 tree 和 blob。请求依次经过节点上的 scion-daemon、区域 scion-cache，再由 scion-server 回源到 Spanner 或对象存储。对象写入后不可变，缓存能够跨任务复用，减少协商、压缩及反复传输。Anthropic 称缓存命中率超过 99%，并限制故障时的回源流量。迁移后，Scion 相较旧 Git 镜像体系的 CPU 和内存需求约缩小 200 倍，检出从分钟级降至秒级，CI 释放约 25% 的 CPU 容量。200 倍说的是基础设施资源占用，并非 Git 操作整体提速。Anthropic 还同步建设 Antique 代码评审、源码搜索、IAM 和批量合并工具，以适配新协议。在线服务的维护也成了新成本。02让数据库读波形，Agent 才能追查故障芯片验证面对的是另一种障碍。

articles.content: 官方承认 3D 短板，跨模型测试 Harness 不同。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       Meta 刚发布的 Muse Wonder，没想到因为一盏熔岩灯，在开发者社区引发了一场关于 AI 模型跑分的争论。10 月 12 日，Meta 推出 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full，主打 Coding Agent、工具调用和长任务执行能力。官方公布的成绩相当亮眼，Wonder Full 在 SWE-Marathon 上拿到 57.5 分，DeepSWE 1.1 达到 79.0 分，已经能够与同期的前沿模型展开竞争。然而，开发者社区 BridgeMind 随后安排了一项 3D 编程测试，要求 Muse Wonder 制作一盏具有透明玻璃外壳、动态熔岩和光照效果的熔岩灯。结果模型只生成了一个红色圆柱体。BridgeMind 随即质疑 Muse Wonder 存在严重的 Benchmaxxing，也就是针对 Benchmark 进行大量优化，成绩看着漂亮，碰上陌生任务却露了怯。连马斯克也忍不住下场，在相关帖子下意味深长地回了一句 Hmm。短短一个词，虽然没有明确表态，却让这场围绕 Meta 新模型的刷分争议又添了几分戏剧性。Meta 首席 AI 官 Alexandr Wang 很快回应，团队确实没有针对 3D 演示游戏进行显式训练，事后看来或许应该补充相关训练，但他仍然希望开发者实际体验 Muse Wonder 的 Coding 能力。雷峰网这场争论有一个重要前提：熔岩灯测试针对的是普通版 Muse Wonder，而 Meta 公布的部分突出成绩来自 Wonder Full，两者存在能力差异。同时，Meta 官方 Model Card 已经明确承认，视觉与空间推理，尤其是 3D 任务，属于 Muse Wonder 的已知短板。但高分模型在陌生任务中遭遇如此明显的失败，依然让人好奇：当前大模型的训练方法究竟在强化哪些能力，Agent Benchmark 又能在多大程度上反映模型的实际水平？01奖励机制，决定模型擅长解决什么问题Muse Wonder 的表现，与当前大模型越来越依赖 Post-training 提升任务能力的技术路线有关。在 Pre-training 阶段，模型通过大规模数据学习语言、代码、空间关系和其他通用知识。进入 Post-training 后，训练会进一步塑造模型的行为策略，尤其是通过强化学习，让它在特定任务环境中形成更稳定的执行能力。Coding Agent 很适合这类训练。例如，给模型一个存在 Bug 的代码仓库，要求它定位问题、修改文件并运行测试。整个过程可以通过编译结果、单元测试和功能检查获得相对明确的反馈。强化学习系统据此判断哪些操作有效，持续强化能够提高任务成功率的行为。训练规模扩大后，模型逐渐学会一套复杂的软件工程策略，包括如何缩小搜索范围、选择工具、处理报错，以及在多轮修改中维护任务状态。Meta 在官方技术文章中提到，Muse Wonder 接受了多样化长任务训练，并引入 Active Focus，使模型能够在遭遇阻碍后尝试其他方案、恢复执行并继续推进任务。但这类训练依赖一个关键条件：环境必须能够向模型提供有用的反馈。熔岩灯恰好打破了传统 Coding Agent 熟悉的反馈方式。雷峰网从程序实现来看，熔岩灯涉及三维几何、透明材质、光照计算和动态形变。如果使用 Three.js，模型需要构造玻璃灯罩，为内部熔岩生成不规则的几何形态，再通过时间变量或噪声函数驱动形状变化。这些代码即使能够正常执行，画面仍然可能完全错误。例如，透明材质的参数配置不当，玻璃就可能变成不透明的实体，熔岩形状缺少连续变化机制，内部效果就可能退化为静态色块。编译器和单元测试很难直接判断这些视觉问题。这意味着，Agent 还需要具备一套

arXiv:2610.22373v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. articles.content:

Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM)-based user encoders serialize heterogeneous behavioral logs and compress them into static representations through autoregressive (AR) prediction. However, their unidirectional constraint limits bidirectional information flow, hindering cross-modal interactions and the joint preservation of multi-source signals. Consequently, the learned static representations struggle to accommodate the distinct evidence requirements of diverse downstream scenarios. articles.title: From Events to Reasoning: Hierarchical Rule Composition over Explicit States
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22403v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What a reasoning system emits is a conclusion; what it owes is a justification. Producing one requires every operation to be admissible on the facts actually available, the dependencies of intermediate results to survive to the end of the path, and the path to be revised when a premise changes. We present the Event Reasoning System (ERS), in which the reasoning state is an explicit event graph. Semantic features nominate candidate objects and rule bindings, and declared rule and task conditions decide which may execute, so candidates that violate the represented period, unit, or evidence constraints cannot enter an accepted reasoning path. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22420v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent-based models are well-suited for modelling agro-ecological systems for decision-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours. In such a context, sensitivity analysis stumbles upon a structural feature of many complex systems: the parameters are not a flat vector but a decision tree in which many parameters appear only when a higher-level choice activates them. Classical global sensitivity analysis presupposes independent inputs over a fixed Cartesian product and is ill-posed on such a branched space and biased by construction. We instead treat the structure of the decisions as a first-class modelling object. articles.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22426v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22441v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. Abstract: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. articles.title: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22460v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue. We argue this is a mistake. Whatever their moral status, models exhibit welfare-like states that causally influence their behaviour. Following recent work, we adopt the term 'functional welfare' for these states. We make three claims. First, functional welfare already arises naturally and will become more robust as models acquire more coherent goals and personas. Second, functional welfare should be treated as a safety variable: it should inform evaluation design, be tracked in monitoring, and be a direct target of post-training. Third, against existing scepticism about measuring AI welfare, we argue that good empirical work on functional welfare is possible. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22466v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22469v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics---ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving long-standing open conjectures---have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve. Yet these successes primarily concern predefined, human-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions. articles.content:

Abstract: Long-term memory enables LLM agents to reuse past experiences, yet retrieving relevant memories does not necessarily provide sufficient evidence for answering a query. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) can integrate understanding and generation within a single backbone. However, it is commonly known that these two capabilities can cause conflicting representations, leading to a central question: how representation and computation should be shared across functionalities? Existing UMMs often rely on a largely fixed structure, where different inputs and functionalities follow the same depth and parameter-sharing pattern. We argue that this assumption is too restrictive: more effective unification requires sharing the computation that supports cross-functional communication while specializing the capacity that becomes task- or input-specific. We introduce FlexUMM, a flexible UMM framework that dynamically decides when to preserve shared computation, when to route specialized capacity, and when to stop further processing. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22380v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. We reopen this design space by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates. Missing positions follow absorbing dynamics, while context undergoes low-rate random substitution, exposing the model to observed but uncertain tokens during training. At inference, a heuristic sampler re-injects noise into suspicious context under an annealed intensity and freezes context updates late in the trajectory. Abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable-specific dynamics and cross-variable interactions. In this work, a Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network (CGDT-CESN) is proposed, which comprises a modular reservoir architecture with each cluster distinctly specializing in one of the variables in the multivariate time series. An innovative reservoir design is proposed in which inter-cluster connections are enabled by empirically observed correlations among variables, providing a data-driven coupling mechanism. Apart from conventional readout training, inter-cluster connection weights informed by correlations are trained, which in turn allows the reservoir to capture time-varying cross-variable dependencies without sacrificing computational efficiency and further improves forecasting accuracy. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22433v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. The root bound certifies a completed schedule's suboptimality gap without a solver. On industry-motivated 10-module prefabricated-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%. Abstract: Distributed Transformer inference across co-located edge devices is fundamentally communication-bound, as exchanging activations between sequence-parallel partitions dominates inference latency under commodity edge bandwidths. Existing compression schemes reduce this cost but retain a structural bottleneck: the received data must still undergo key/value projection before attention can proceed, serializing computation behind communication. Trace places a Vector Quantizer (VQ) at the post-attention residual of every Transformer layer and precomputes codebook-indexed key/value representations. Abstract: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22438v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine-tunes without alignment content. Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below. Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail. Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting remains a challenge in supervised continual learning, as adapting to new tasks causes representation drift and loss of previously learned information. Replay examples specify where the constraints apply, while leading right singular directions of the encoder Jacobian specify which changes are penalized. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22467v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities. One prominent approach is self-distillation, where a model is trained to match the token-level predictions it would have produced when given access to additional context, such as a cue, feedback, or instruction. However, the safety properties of this training procedure are poorly understood. In this paper, we present a surprising safety failure of recursive self-distillation, where each self-distilled model becomes the teacher for the next round of training. We observe that when a safe model is recursively self-distilled on its own (safe) generations while receiving an additional non-harmful cue, it becomes increasingly misaligned across a diverse set of harmful queries; we call this Progressive Misalignment. articles.title: Generative Value Classifier
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22497v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Q-learning is premised on learning a function to predict the value of a state-action pair, with the goal of using such a function to guide policy improvement. Most approaches learn this function from scratch using scalar or distributional return targets. This discriminative approach leaves another source of supervision for learning representations unused: the actions themselves. Rather than directly predict the return of a state-action pair, we ask the reverse question: how likely is the action under each possible return? This perspective provides a critic whose generative component is a return-conditioned policy, which can share the actor's architecture. Training this policy supervises the critic with every action rather than with returns alone, and a squared-error loss anchors the critic's Q-value to the bootstrapped target. Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from privileged information (PI) without a separate teacher model. Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Abstract: Data-driven approaches often face ambiguity in datasets due to sensor or target noise, insufficient information, and noise in the input data. Abstract: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. REALCLI provides two modes for paired comparison: REALCLI-EXEC supplies complete specifications upfront, whereas REALCLI-COLLAB introduces a scripted user that delivers progressive information, corrections, constraint revisions, and authorization decisions. articles.title: AuditKIT: A Unified Evaluation Spine for Benchmarking, Judging, and Comparing Large Language Models and Agentic Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating language models and agents requires combining benchmark accuracy, judge-based assessment, runtime performance, tool-use behavior, and retrieval quality. Differences in interfaces, metric semantics, and trace formats complicate these comparisons and can hide failures in agentic workflows. We present AuditKIT, a source-available evaluation library that records these measurements in one result representation, with direction-aware metric contracts, configuration fingerprints, and extensible metrics and backends. For agents, it provides turn-aware tool-call matching, separates parallel from sequential execution, and distinguishes verified task outcomes from trajectory-level diagnostics. Missing or unobservable evidence is marked unscored rather than counted as failure. articles.title: alkhder at ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks: Constrained Selection and Rotation-Averaged Logit Scoring for Multimodal Hallucination Detection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22515v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We describe our submission to Subtask~1b of ImageEval 2026. The task consists of selecting the single visually valid statement from three candidates paired with an image, and is in both English and Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). Our system uses a pre-trained 7B vision--language model in a zero-shot setting, without task-specific training or fine-tuning. We formulate the task as a constrained selection problem and choose the answer using next-token log-probabilities. To reduce answer-position bias, we apply a Latin-square rotation to the candidate statements. Our system achieves CI scores of 0.0510 on the English test set and 0.0960 on the MSA test set, reducing CI relative to the official 3B baselines reported on devtest by 83.7\% and 80.4\%, respectively.

articles.title: Learning User Representations to Improve Simulation Fidelity
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: User simulators enable interactive training and evaluation of AI assistants at scale. Yet current simulators struggle to reproduce the diverse behaviors of real users, leading to assistants that generalize poorly to underrepresented users. We identify user representations as an underexplored bottleneck in user simulation. User representations are natural-language descriptions that condition simulators to reproduce a particular user's behavior. A representation's quality becomes apparent in hindsight, through the behavior it induces in a simulator. To evaluate and optimize user representations, we formulate a conversation reconstruction task: given an original conversation, we generate a representation, condition a simulator on it, simulate a conversation, and then measure fidelity by comparing user behavior in the original and simulated conversations. articles.title: alkhder at AlexandriaX-2026: Context-Aware English-to-Dialectal Arabic Dialogue Translation with QLoRA-Fine-Tuned NileChat-3B
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22525v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper describes team Alkhder's submission to Subtask 1 of the AlexandriaX-2026 shared task, which asks systems to translate English dialogue turns into thirteen Arabic dialects. We fine-tune NileChat-3B-Base with QLoRA on the Alexandria parallel dialogue corpus, training one set of adapter weights for all dialects. Each turn is translated conditioned on the target country and dialect, the domain, the participant roles, the speaker-addressee gender direction, and the preceding dialogue context. At inference, conversations are translated autoregressively and the model is fed its own previous outputs back as context without using any gold target-side test information. Under the constrained track, using only Alexandria data, it trains in about one hour and translates the private test set in under two hours. The system reaches a country-macro-averaged spBLEU of 20.36 and chrF++ of 36.64 on both tracks.

articles.content:

Abstract: Decision models, non-generative scorers that report a probability over caller-supplied options and emit no text, are increasingly deployed as routers, classifiers and guardrails. Because they generate nothing, rationales and chain-of-thought do not apply. We audit three: an encoder scorer, a decoder scorer and a closed API, entirely through interventions on their input, using expert-annotated Bengali idioms carrying a gold figurative and a gold literal gloss. Dropping an idiom's own literal gloss into the option list draws every arm toward it, taking 65% to 96% of each arm's remaining Bengali errors. articles.title: Pearl-Chat: Engineering a native Luganda language model from first principles in JAX and Flax NNX
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive foundation language models predominantly target high-resource Indo-European languages, imposing computational and morphological penalties on under-represented African languages. Generic multilingual tokenizers routinely exceed fertility rates of 3.2 tokens per word on agglutinative Bantu languages, degrading context efficiency and inflating latency. We present Pearl-Chat, an 8,473,122-parameter ($\sim$8.5M) causal decoder-only transformer engineered for Luganda (Oluganda, ISO 639-2: lg), a low-resource Niger-Congo Bantu language spoken by over 10 million people in East Africa. Built from first mathematical principles in JAX and Flax NNX, Pearl-Chat uses explicit functional state decomposition (nnx.split and nnx.merge), deterministic resumable data streaming via Google Grain, and SPMD tensor parallelism using jax.sharding.Mesh. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in English Relation Extraction (RE) tasks, a significant gap remains in assessing their RE performance in low-resource languages, due to a lack of standardized benchmarks. Creating native, language-specific annotated RE benchmarks is expensive and requires human expertise, while relying on translation yields suboptimal, inaccurate datasets that introduce English-centric biases. To tackle this, we propose a scalable, language-agnostic methodology to create RE data by denoising naturally occurring yet noisy alignments of knowledge bases and corresponding texts. We define a proper alignment via a Natural Language Inference (NLI) task, where a relation triplet is entailed by an input text. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22545v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stereotypes are subjective constructs that are mediated by the cultural context in which they are viewed. Successfully modeling them thus also requires cultural competence. When using large language models (LLMs) for stereotype-related tasks, such as their detection, it is therefore crucial that models can access relevant cultural knowledge and adjust responses accordingly. Since LLMs have shown disparities in what cultural knowledge is available to them, their capacity regarding stereotypes may also be disparate across languages and cultural contexts (e.g., for non-English languages or for non-US contexts). In this paper, we systematically investigate the effectiveness of LLMs for culture-specific stereotype detection across three factors: (1) the prompting language, (2) the instruction tuning language, and (3) the fine-tuning dataset size. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Successful completion of perspectivist natural language processing (NLP) annotation tasks requires algorithms to be aligned across diverse perspectives in order to predict how different humans will rate text. This work studies how the performance of such algorithms varies for annotators who behave differently than others, either by providing annotations that diverge from others' responses or by providing fewer annotations altogether. To aid with characterizing model performance, we curate the largest collection to date of perspectivist NLP datasets with ordinal annotations. After evaluating multiple classes of perspectivist algorithms across each of the datasets, we model the relationship between individual annotator idiosyncrasy and algorithm performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22586v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups. Using the HateXplain dataset, we introduce Plausibility-EFG, a metric that measures the largest difference in explanation plausibility across demographic groups by comparing model-generated token attributions with human-annotated rationales. We evaluate BERT, RoBERTa, and ADV-RoBERTa, an adversarially trained model, using Integrated Gradients and SHAP. Our results show that ADV-RoBERTa improves classification performance and alignment between explanations and human rationales while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups. articles.title: SAG2: Embedding-Free Multi-Hop Retrieval with BM25 and JEV
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Strong multi-hop retrieval should be practical to deploy without expensive corpus preparation or complex database infrastructure. We present SAG2, an embedding-free retrieval architecture built around a single SQLite database, BM25, and contextual evidence decisions from JEV. SAG2 follows the query-time association principle of SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), while replacing its event-entity and dense indexes with a lexical index over original passages. Selected passages supply terms for further retrieval, and newly retrieved evidence guides subsequent decisions. This moves semantic evidence selection to query time, eliminating offline embedding computation, LLM-based event-entity extraction, and dedicated database servers. articles.title: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22594v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical multi-agent systems, in which LLM agents discuss a case, are increasingly studied for clinical decision support. Prompt injection, text that an attacker adds to a model's input, can manipulate LLMs into wrong decisions. How it affects these systems, and how to protect them, remains unclear. Across two systems, two model families and three benchmarks, a single injected passage succeeds in up to 61% of cases, and collaboration does not consistently protect against it. Existing defenses help only partly: they miss injections that look like ordinary clinical text. Yet when asked to check the injected text against the patient's findings, a model that followed the injection usually rejects it. We therefore propose a training-free defense that verifies the clinical judgments behind the system's decision. Abstract: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models must efficiently find identifiers across diverse contexts while maintaining a low false-positive rate (FPR) on high-volume traffic. Recent detectors increasingly rely on complex architectures that raise deployment cost, yet many are fine-tuned on only a few synthetic datasets that limit their coverage. Combining public datasets is challenging because their taxonomies differ, and even after categories are mapped to a common schema, labels can disagree on what counts as a detection, producing inconsistent training and evaluation signals. To address these problems, we present a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based detector trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a detailed definition of broad contextual detection for 12 structured PII categories. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Uncertainty can measure hallucination risk in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), but only when retrieved evidence constrains the answer. When evidence is present, unsupported factual claims become less likely; when retrieval coverage is poor, the model can answer from internal knowledge and assign high probability to unsupported claims. We test this across four instruction-tuned models on HotpotQA and SQuAD. After matching faithful and hallucinated answers within word-count bins, length-only classifiers fall near chance, while perplexity reaches 0.81--0.91 AUROC on targeted unsupported edits. Varying retrieval depth shows why the score changes meaning: detection can weaken with only the top-ranked passage, then recover after adding a second passage. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22618v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models rely on spurious features in clinical classification: swapping a single gender token in clinical notes alters gender-irrelevant diagnoses in up to 53.5% of cases. Existing inference-time corrections either need counterfactual data built around the specific spurious feature or behave unpredictably. We observe that how a model's preference between answers evolves across layers, its prediction trajectory, indicates for each document whether a correction is likely to help. We propose Trajectory-Guided Steering (TGS), which decides from the trajectory alone whether to correct each prediction and in which direction, with no counterfactual data and no knowledge of the spurious feature. Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly serve as judges in training and evaluation pipelines, often assessing answers together with explanations. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22444v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). In this paper, we introduce Event-STVG, a task that shifts STVG from locating what is described toward event-level reasoning by unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding. To facilitate research on Event-STVG, we construct a large-scale benchmark comprising 4,016 annotated event occurrences across soccer and seven additional domains. Abstract: Human communication is inherently multimodal, conveying intent not only through linguistic and vocal cues but also through visual signals. Abstract: Reliable 3D person detection is important for rescue robotics to give first responders situational awareness. Yet most multimodal 3D detection research targets automotive scenarios in which pedestrians mostly appear in a narrow range of upright, near-road poses. It is therefore unclear how much of the reported performance transfers to rescue settings, as a person may be lying, partially occluded, or in unstructured indoor and outdoor environments. Abstract: Diffusion models have become a leading approach in visual generative modeling, particularly effective in text-to-image and controllable generation. articles.title: CFC26: Building Evaluations for Deployment in Sonar-Based Fish Counting
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate counts of fish populations are essential for monitoring ecosystems and making decisions for conservation, harvest limits, and river management. In many field deployments, these counts are obtained from sonar videos that experts must inspect manually, making large-scale monitoring slow, expensive, and difficult. Automated counting systems have been proposed as a scalable alternative, but so far this promise has been difficult to realize in deployment. Developing evaluations that better reflect real-world deployment conditions will help close this gap and drive improvements in counting performance in practice. To achieve this, we propose Caltech Fish Counting 2026 (CFC26), a new dataset with improved evaluation protocols that simulate deployment to seen and novel rivers, testing in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance. articles.title: Seeing Seizures: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Video and EEG Deep Learning for Automated Rodent Seizure Detection and Severity Grading
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22566v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manual annotation of synchronized video and EEG recordings is a bottleneck in preclinical seizure research. We present an empirical study of seizure detection and behavioral severity grading using 24,131 paired clips from 601 sessions across 20 rats in a soman-induced epilepsy model. Ten video architectures and seven single-channel EEG models are evaluated independently on binary detection and three- and five-class severity tasks. In the session-exclusive reference comparison, R(2+1)D-18 and GRU achieve detection macro-F1 scores of 0.968 and 0.974, respectively; for five-class grading, the corresponding scores are 0.657 and 0.560. Subject-exclusive evaluation reduces five-class macro-F1 to 0.475 for video and 0.404 for EEG, highlighting the difficulty of grading unseen animals. articles.title: Stuck on Shuffle: On Attribute-Object Binding in Vision-Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22602v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval is a fundamental task in multimodal systems: given an image or text query, the goal is to find the most relevant images or texts in a collection, often using a shared embedding space. Reliable retrieval requires these embeddings to capture not only which concepts are present, but also how they are composed. One key compositional challenge is attribute--object binding: encoding which attributes belong to which objects. Existing benchmarks provide a limited view of this capability, typically covering a subset of modality pairings, simple two-object swaps, or small attribute sets. Consequently, it remains unclear how robustly current models preserve attribute--object bindings across different modality pairings and more complex settings. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22606v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: FOR-species20K is the largest public LiDAR benchmark for tree-species classification, pooling 25 independently collected terrestrial, mobile, and airborne laser-scanning datasets across 33 species. We introduce a multi-resolution, multi-view ConvNeXtV2 model that improves official hidden-test accuracy from 79.5% to 85.0%, ranking first at the time of submission. We then examine what this score measures. Because the hidden test is species-balanced, its overall accuracy is more comparable to a macro metric than to accuracy under the public set's long-tailed distribution. Moreover, the official random split places every source dataset in both training and evaluation. A logistic probe recovers source identity from out-of-fold model probabilities with 69% accuracy, while geometric features identify the source above 90% within two widely shared species; 18 of the 33 species occur in only one source. articles.title: ProactGen: Learning Proactive Clarification for Video Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22608v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in video generation let users create high-quality videos from natural language descriptions, yet obtaining results that match user intent remains time-consuming: individual generations are computationally expensive, and underspecified prompts force repeated cycles of generation, inspection, and revision. Existing video prompt optimization methods improve generation through automatic rewriting, but cannot supply the ideas and preferences that were not in the initial description. We propose ProactGen, a video generation framework that learns proactive clarification, eliciting user intent through questions grounded in generated video drafts. articles.title: Shift-Reliance Alignment: Ranking Vision-Language Models by the Cues They Trust
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22610v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are usually chosen from leaderboards, which give one ranking for every application. On questions about objects that a scene suggests but does not contain, however, the model with the lowest error on the POPE hallucination benchmark is not the one with the lowest error on such questions. For yes/no questions about object presence, we show that the best model for a target domain can be predicted without running any candidate on that domain, given 650 to 1,200 labeled target items that calibrate a detector. We measure each model's reliance on a cue, a feature such as scene context or text in the image, by editing 100 labeled source images so that the cue suggests the wrong answer, and comparing with a matched control edit. articles.title: Deep Learning for Deepfake Image Detection: Comparative Model Evaluation and Gradient-Based Visual Attribution
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22676v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthetic facial imagery has made the distinction between authentic and generated content increasingly important for digital forensics and online trust. This study examines an explainable deep-learning workflow for image-level deepfake detection using two contrasting classification strategies: a compact convolutional model trained from scratch and an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 model adapted through two-stage transfer learning. Experiments were conducted with the balanced 140k Real and Fake Faces dataset, comprising 140,000 facial images. Under the recorded validation protocol, the augmented from-scratch model reached 84.15% accuracy (loss 0.3625), compared with 95.90% accuracy (loss 0.1074) for the fine-tuned pretrained model. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Answering complex spatial reasoning questions from egocentric video requires determining what evidence is needed, acquiring targeted observations, and combining them through multiple reasoning steps. Existing vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to perform this process reliably. Agentic systems address this challenge by querying external vision and geometry tools, but training their reasoning leaves these tools unchanged, so inaccurate observations can still lead to incorrect answers. We introduce EgoP$^{2}$C, a framework that internalizes a plan-perceive-compose process within a single VLM. To this end, we first train specialized Planner and Perception teachers using separate adapters (Dual-LoRA), then fine-tune the corresponding experts in a mixture-of-experts (MoE) student under their supervision. articles.title: Thinking from Above: Efficient Spatial Reasoning with Bird's-Eye-View Visual Tokens
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22700v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) organize observations primarily in time, but embodied spatial reasoning requires organizing them in space. Consequently, their visual representations can remain locally consistent across nearby frames while lacking a persistent spatial context that is stable across viewpoints and time. We exploit depth and camera pose, which are naturally available to embodied agents, to explicitly establish this spatial correspondence. We introduce Cambrian-BEV, which extends Cambrian-S with a parameter-free geometric tokenization scheme that back-projects visual patch features from each frame into a shared bird's-eye-view (BEV) coordinate frame and averages features that fall within the same spatial cell. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22720v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-fidelity 3D generative modeling underpins game asset creation, medical imaging, and VR/AR environmental design, where geometric structure directly influences perception and decision-making. Diffusion models represent a powerful paradigm for point cloud generation. However, existing approaches rely heavily on local voxel or patch features and often miss global structural organization, and much less work has studied how global conditioning can be used to improve generation quality. In this paper, we introduce HilbertGen-3D, a novel topology-aware conditional diffusion framework based on Hilbert-Multifractal Conditioning (HMC). HMC computes multi-scale voxel measures, serializes them via a 3D Hilbert curve to expose structured spatial dependencies, and estimates the generalized fractal dimensions from scale-dependent partition functions. articles.title: Improving OCR Accuracy Through Multi-Classifier Verification of Visually Similar Characters
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22726v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distinguishing visually similar characters is a persistent challenge for optical character recognition (OCR) systems, causing errors in critical applications of text digitization. While preprocessing techniques improve image quality and word-level post-processing corrects spelling errors, neither addresses character-level visual ambiguity, an intrinsic property of certain character pairs that limits even state-of-the-art OCR models. We present the Character Verification Model (CVM), a character-level post-processing framework that verifies and corrects ambiguous characters in OCR outputs using specialized binary classifiers trained on visually confusable pairs such as 'O'/'0', 'Z'/'2', and 'S'/'5'. CVM operates independently of dictionary validation, making it suitable for non-lexical data including serial numbers, alphanumeric codes, and license plates. articles.content:

Abstract: Creative intent in video editing can be expressed through text instructions (e.g., "remove the people"), image references (e.g., subject appearance), video references (e.g., camera movement), or a combination of the above. We introduce OmniXRef, a unified framework for multimodal multi-reference video editing that allows users to combine variable numbers of text, image, and video references to control diverse attributes of a source video. We first devise a unified input design with a reference-bank interface and introduce $R^2$-RoPE to support generalization to more references. Then our model, OmniXRef-Model, uses a single-stream diffusion transformer to jointly process the source video and multimodal context from an MLLM in an interleaved sequence. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving. Generative world models can expand scenarios and predict future observations, yet may introduce content unsupported by measurements. We propose DriveWorld3D, a framework combining temporal video learning, measurement constraints from multiple sensors, and offline generative simulation. Its online component maintains a unified world state comprising road surfaces, volumetric occupancy, dynamic entities, and road relations, while separately representing physical occupancy, observability, and evidence provenance. articles.title: Mothership: A Two Tier Autonomous Refuse Collection System for Pedestrian Campuses
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Refuse collection in pedestrian campuses, parks and mixed-use districts remains manual because compaction trucks cannot reach bins located on walkways, courtyards and building service doors. This paper presents Mothership, a two-tier autonomous refuse collection system in which an electric compaction truck (the mothership) carries two low-speed sidewalk robots (RoboCarts) that fetch standard two-wheel bins, deliver them to the truck, return the empty bins to their original positions and re-dock on the truck for charging. The architecture separates responsibilities by scale: the truck performs road driving, compaction, lifting and energy supply, while the carts perform only sidewalk transport and bin grasping. This split removes the lift-and-tip mechanism from the sidewalk vehicle, keeping it light and low, and relaxes cart-to-truck docking tolerance to the +/-100 mm capture window of a standard automated lifter. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22471v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22496v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot learning has advanced by scaling demonstration datasets and model capacity; however, deploying a new robot embodiment or task typically necessitates a dedicated teleoperation corpus. The resulting policies remain bounded by their imitation distributions, limiting generalization and continual self-improvement. We introduce RAX (Robot Agent eXploration), an open-source framework for robot agents centered on scaling exploration: enabling agents to improve by acquiring online experience and synthesizing executable programs. In RAX, a general-purpose coding agent generates robot control code, operating without action demonstration data, hand-engineered action primitives, or value-function guidance. Through online exploration, the agent identifies decision sequences that achieve task goals and compiles them into modular programs encapsulating the full perception-planning-control loop. articles.title: RTISSLAM-3D: Full 6-DoF SLAM With an In-Air 3D Imaging Sonar
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22552v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Echolocating bats navigate dense forests using sonar alone, and in-air 3D imaging sonars now capture the entire frontal hemisphere with every pulse. Sonar SLAM, however, has so far been planar: current systems estimate a 2D trajectory and discard the elevation information in the sonar images, an assumption that does not hold on rough and sloped terrain such as a forest floor. In this paper, we introduce RTISSLAM-3D, a novel 6-DoF SLAM system for a wheeled robot that carries an in-air 3D imaging sonar, an IMU and wheel encoders. A CFAR detector on the sphere reduces every sonar image to a sparse set of 3D detections, which we use for a 3D acoustic odometry that models the shape of the sonar beam, for place recognition with polar submap descriptors, and for the verification of loop closures by 3D registration, all combined in a 6-DoF pose graph with attitude factors. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon, multi-stage Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often require visual information that is no longer present in the current observation. Retaining the complete observation history is computationally expensive and highly redundant, motivating selective visual memory. We introduce RePlanMem-VLA (Replanning-Guided Keyframe Memory for VLA), which turns a policy's own plan revisions into an online memory-write signal. Under receding-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions. RePlanMem-VLA treats unusually large disagreement between these temporally aligned predictions as evidence of a task-relevant event. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single-task autoregressive decoder-only and Flow-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ policies over MIKASA-Robo-VLA tasks. articles.content:

Abstract: We demonstrate high-precision global localization using natural ground texture viewed through microscope optics, achieving localization in the tens-of-micrometers regime. Leveraging this relationship, we then develop a microscope-based localization system that addresses the calibration, camera-modeling, and focus challenges introduced by high-magnification imaging. We evaluate this system across several surface textures using a calibrated precision gantry. Across 1,007 held-out queries per surface, the system localizes every query and achieves translation RMSEs of 28$-$73 $\mu$m. Abstract: Flow-based policies such as $\pi_0$ are trained on a fixed set of embodiments, and transferring them to new ones is an open problem. To adapt a frozen $\pi_0$ to a new embodiment without additional demonstrations or parameter updates, we train a lightweight embodiment classifier to distinguish successful action chunks on the source body from those on the target body, using a few calibration tasks. articles.content:

Abstract: Quadruped parkour policies handle canonical obstacles well, but their training curricula often miss the irregular, compound geometry of industrial and disaster-response sites, where agile locomotion matters most. Such environments pose a hard generalization problem: even training directly on reconstructed geometry from the target site does not reliably yield policies that traverse it. Hand-designed curricula span only a few terrain families, and recent LLM-generated curricula offer little control over which policy weaknesses they target. We propose FCTS, a failure-conditioned terrain curriculum framework that uses localized traversal failures to automatically generate the terrains a policy should train on next. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22670v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-robot authoring can reduce completion time by distributing drawing work, but the resulting speedup depends on task structure and the allocation-routing pipeline. We investigate these relationships by representing drawings as geometric stroke graphs and comparing component-level (single-token) allocation with shared-token (decomposed) allocation, which permits multiple robots to work within a connected component. A simulation study of 385 drawings and teams of one to eight robots shows diminishing speedup gains under single-token allocation and larger mean speedups under the shared-token pipeline, each normalized by its own single-robot completion time. Shared-token execution also exhibits lower idle-time shares at larger team sizes, although it does not reduce completion time for every drawing. articles.content:

Abstract: Spatial memory enables robots to reuse past observations for localization, navigation, and question answering. Designing such memory involves jointly deciding what to retain and how to retrieve it for diverse semantic, metric, and temporal needs. We investigate whether coding agents can automate this design process through iterative implementation and evaluation. Under a fixed development budget, a Designer Agent writes and revises code for memory construction and retrieval using feedback from a fixed Query Agent. The resulting implementations are frozen before building memories from held-out observation histories, without access to downstream questions, and evaluated across five complementary task tracks using the same Query Agent. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22762v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rigid-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments. This coupling makes planning chal- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry. We propose Shape- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel-time, or cost- to-go, representation for rigid-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses. Abstract: Precise pedicel-targeted grasping in strawberry harvesting remains a critical bottleneck due to the pedicel's small diameter (1.3-3 mm), color similarity with surrounding foliage, and precise force control required for clean abscission zone detachment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22812v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires not only understanding instructions but also determining whether and how a robot can physically execute them. However, existing VLN benchmarks typically assume executable instructions and focus on long-horizon tasks. This leaves body-dependent local execution, including passability and collision-free execution, largely unexamined. Evaluating these factors within long-horizon tasks would entangle local physical execution with task planning and long-term spatial memory, making navigation failures difficult to attribute. We therefore focus on grounding local navigation commands in executable motion under environmental and robot body constraints. articles.title: Simultaneous Force and Motion Control in Generalised Coordinates
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22813v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot manipulators often come into contact with rigid objects when performing work. This imposes physical constraints on their motion. Simultaneous force & motion control was developed to regulate contact forces commensurate with these constraints, whilst projecting motion control in to the orthogonal, unconstrained directions. This is typically formulated in the task coordinates, i.e. operational space, then mapped to joint torques to command the robot. However, most constraints on the robot control, such as joint limits, collision avoidance, singularity avoidance, etc. are naturally expressed in generalised coordinates (joint space). Thus, formulating the control problem in task space makes it difficult to guarantee control feasibility. In this paper Gauss' principle of least constraint is used to solve the control as a quadratic programming (QP) problem in generalised coordinates. articles.title: DefFlow: Goal-Conditioned Deformable Object Manipulation using 3D Point Flows
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating deformable objects toward desired 3D configurations is a fundamental capability for robots operating in unstructured physical environments. However, as the range of possible initial and target configurations grows, goal-conditioned deformable manipulation requires a robot to infer increasingly diverse manipulation behaviors in addition to precise continuous actions. We introduce DefFlow, a framework for goal-conditioned manipulation of deformable objects toward a broad range of 3D configurations. DefFlow learns from demonstrations by jointly predicting the goal-conditioned 3D point flow of the robot and deformable object. We show that this formulation better captures both the manipulation decisions, such as when and where to grasp, release, or re-grasp, and the precise continuous motions required for goal reaching, rather than predicting only the robot flow. articles.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Policy Improvement via Flow-Reversed Action Anchors
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22852v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generalist robot policies offer strong behavioral priors, but achieving deployment-level reliability and throughput remains difficult. Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve these policies, yet its effectiveness is constrained by the cost of online interaction. Existing methods adapt frozen flow-matching policies by treating noise space as a continuous action space. We show that this behaviorally unstructured space makes exploration inefficient, often preventing these methods from extracting meaningful learning signals on challenging tasks. We introduce AnchorQ, which enables coarse-to-fine policy improvement through a structured, refinable latent action representation. articles.title: Structured Perception Representations for Off-road Dynamics Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomously navigating off-road terrain at high speed demands accurate control, which often relies on dynamics models that capture complex interactions between the robot and terrain. In off-road regimes, terrain interaction is a major component of the vehicle's dynamics. Prior work attempts to capture this effect by training learned models of the vehicle's dynamics, conditioned on its perception of the local environment. However, said conditioning is often overly simplistic, ignoring the spatial structure of the dynamics problem. Our approach, SpatialBEV, exploits this spatial structure. At each step, we query the bird's-eye-view (BEV) features around the predicted state, conditioning the next prediction on current geometric and semantic cues. articles.title: SenseSwarm: Swarm Exploration via Neural Structure Estimation with Shared World-Anticipation for Rapid Mapping
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A robot swarm covers a building faster with more robots, but the map is only as complete as the space the robots have physically visited. We target the amount of an unknown building a decentralized swarm knows at each instant, ahead of physical coverage. SenseSwarm serves a lightweight learned map predictor on the swarm's shared occupancy map and folds the predicted structure back into a stigmergic guidance field. Its 709K-parameter predictor is fine-tuned on the swarm's own multi-front observations, which we show is necessary: a single-robot predictor collapses on such views. articles.title: Ego2Contact: Predicting Touch from Egocentric Human Video for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22932v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Contact locations and interaction forces are critical for contact-rich robot manipulation but are often ambiguous from vision alone. Measuring them on robots requires specialized tactile hardware and platform-specific data collection, which keeps robot tactile data scarce. Human egocentric video is far easier to scale but lacks touch. Recent predictors trained on egocentric recordings paired with tactile-glove measurements can predict this missing signal from video alone. These predictors, however, remain confined to human hands, which differ from robot hands in appearance and tactile layout. We present Ego2Contact, which learns a visual-tactile prior from human interactions and transfers it to robot hands. articles.title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
articles.content: Generated videos often lose geometric consistency under camera motion: structures warp under viewpoint change, parallax becomes inconsistent, and smooth camera movement may collapse into shot-like transitions. We argue that this failure is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. To address this, we propose Video Geometry Corrector (VGC), a post-hoc video-to-video model trained on synthetic paired supervision. Starting from real videos with diverse camera motion and pose annotations, we construct VG-Pairs with a synthetic paired-supervision data generation pipeline. Each video clip is treated as a geometry-consistent target and paired with a distorted counterpart synthesized by a pretrained image-to-video inpainting model using trajectory-adaptive keyframes. VGC learns to map the distorted input to the geometry-consistent target without modifying the source generator, and uses optical flow as an auxiliary cue to help disentangle camera motion from object motion. Experiments on pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks show that VGC improves geometric consistency across multiple source generators, and scaling to a larger backbone further extends the framework toward more general video refinement.

articles.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.

articles.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
articles.content: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich assembly, where the robot must find a millimeter-scale opening, mesh gear teeth, or catch a thread through light contact? We study this question by training blind assembly policies that observe only a short history of joint positions, velocities, and their own actions, without visual, force, torque, or tactile sensing. The poses of both the fixture and the part are unknown to the policy, and the grasp is randomized substantially. The policy must therefore assemble the parts through contact, sensed exclusively through its own proprioception. Trained with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts, such policies learn peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading. The peg insertion policy transfers zero-shot to the real world and inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 73% of trials. Controlled comparisons with matched visual policies in simulation show that blind policies generalize far better to unseen part shapes and sizes, though they can be slower. Training such policies needs thousands of different assemblies, each simulated with its clearance intact, so we also release an open-source generator that builds them procedurally from exact convex pieces for MuJoCo; it is more accurate and faster than convex decomposition or MuJoCo's signed-distance collision. Videos and interactive simulations are at https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/.
